title: Solid, Liquid & Gas Fuels
description: Fuels come in three states of matter. Sort them all to reclaim the next ember of the Guardian Flame.

content.value: Fuels can be classified by their physical state into SOLID, LIQUID, and GASEOUS fuels. Each type is suited to different uses.

SOLID FUELS      LIQUID FUELS       GASEOUS FUELS
🪵  wood          ⛽  petrol          🔥  LPG (cooking gas)
🪨  coal          🛢️  diesel          🚗  CNG (vehicles)
🔥  charcoal      🪔  kerosene        💧  hydrogen
🐄  dung cake                         🏭  natural gas

Solid fuels like wood and coal are cheap and were used for centuries, but they produce a lot of smoke and ash. Liquid fuels like petrol, diesel and kerosene store lots of energy in a small space, which is why vehicles use them.

Gaseous fuels like LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas, used for cooking) and CNG (Compressed Natural Gas, used in vehicles) are generally the CLEANEST. They burn completely, produce little smoke, and are easy to control with a tap or valve. That's why homes and modern buses increasingly use them.
LPG is your home cooking gas; CNG powers cleaner buses and cars. Gaseous fuels burn cleaner than solids and liquids, so cities use them to reduce pollution.
Key Takeaway: Fuels are classified as solid (wood, coal), liquid (petrol, diesel, kerosene), or gaseous (LPG, CNG, hydrogen). Gaseous fuels are usually the cleanest and easiest to control.

quiz.question: Which of these is a GASEOUS fuel?
quiz.explain: LPG (cooking gas) is a gaseous fuel. Coal is solid and kerosene is liquid.

quiz.question: Compared with solid fuels, gaseous fuels generally…
quiz.explain: Gaseous fuels burn completely and cleanly, producing little smoke — a key advantage.

quiz.question: CNG, used to run cleaner buses and cars, stands for…
quiz.explain: CNG is Compressed Natural Gas, a cleaner gaseous fuel for vehicles.
